advisory.finding: `record_parent_divergence` appends a bridge_alerts record unconditionally with no `alert_store.is_deduped` gate, so a persistently unrepresentable/rejected parent — which is re-emitted every reconcile pass in steady state — re-files a new alert every pass (~20 min) indefinitely, flooding the alert channel. Every other alert site in this package dedupes across passes over the 24h window.
merged_from: The alert record stores `"key": key` (the raw issue key, e.g. 'DIG-100') rather than a compound dedup key. `alert_store.is_deduped` matches on `rec.get("key")`, so even if a dedup gate were added, using the bare issue key would collide across the three distinct kinds (outbound-parent-unrepresentable / -rejected / -failed) for the same issue, and would also collide with any other alert type that keys on the same issue key.
scenarios: A DC deployment that cannot represent an epic-link parent (outbound-parent-unrepresentable) — the same issue fails set_parent on every pass and files a duplicate alert every ~20 minutes
An 8b25 HTTP 400 hierarchy rejection that persists across passes
advisory.suggested_fix: Build a compound dedup_key (e.g. `f"{kind}:{key}:{parent}"`), consult `_load_alert_store().is_deduped(dedup_key, repo_root=repo_root)` before appending, and write that dedup_key as the record's `"key"` (see fetcher.py:223-236 / run_differs.py:101-114).
